hero.title: Automated GC-MS Data Analysis Across Instrument Formats
hero.intro: Upload one sample's GC-MS peak table and a standard file (target list). The page detects the table format, unifies compound names and CAS numbers, handles duplicate peaks and peaks with several library hits by fixed rules, finds the relative content of each target, then uses odor thresholds to compute OAV or ROAV, rank the key flavor compounds and draw a flavor profile.
scope.text: This site is built for quickly processing a single sample: upload one file containing the peak table of one sample at a time. To process hundreds or thousands of samples in batch, please email
scope.upload: One sample at a time: each file should contain the peak table of one sample.
scope.multi: This file has {n} samples. The site handles one at a time; choose one above. For batch processing, email
privacy.lead: Your data never leaves your computer.
privacy.text: Everything runs in your browser and files are never uploaded to any server. The page has no analytics or tracking, so it suits a first look at confidential company data.
privacy.v1: Method 1: once the page has loaded, disconnect from the network (turn off Wi-Fi or unplug the cable), then upload and analyze a file. Everything still works.
privacy.v2: Method 2: press F12 to open the developer tools, go to the Network panel, then upload and analyze a file. No data requests appear.
privacy.tech: The page's Content-Security-Policy only allows connections to this site; the browser blocks requests to anywhere else. Templates and settings you save stay in your own browser.
privacy.mini: Read in your browser only, never uploaded
import.title: Import data
import.peak_short: Columns: compound name or CAS · retention time · peak area or relative content (%); add a concentration column if quantified (used for OAV).
about.peak_required: The peak table needs three columns: (1) compound name or CAS number; (2) retention time; (3) peak area or relative content (%). If the sample was quantified, add a concentration column; it is used when OAV is chosen. Retention index, match score and peak number columns are optional. Columns are recognized from header keywords or instrument templates, and you can correct them in the step "Check the header and columns".

tol.merge_help: Rule 1: adjacent peaks of the same compound closer than this are merged (areas added). Larger values merge more.

result.title: Result
result.summary: {n} targets in the standard file: {found} found ({manual} assigned by you), {miss} not found. Target window ± {win} min, adjacent-peak merge tolerance {merge}.
result.rel_column: Relative content is taken from the peak table's relative content column; for peaks merged by rule 1 the values are added.
result.rel_area: No relative content column in the peak table: relative content = peak area ÷ sum of all peak areas × 100.
log.title: Processing log
log.merged: {name}: the adjacent peaks at {rt1} and {rt2} min are the same compound and no farther apart than the merge tolerance of {tol} min; merged (areas added, retention time of the larger peak).
log.not_adjacent: {name} appears at {rt1} and {rt2} min with other compounds in between; not merged, one of them may be a misidentification.
log.closest_of_several: {target}: several peaks with the same identification in the window ({rts} min); the one closest to the reference retention time, {kept} min, is used.
log.peak_to_closer_target: The peak at {rt} min fits both "{target}" and "{kept}"; it goes to "{kept}", whose reference retention time is closer, and "{target}" counts as not found.
log.hit_chosen: The library gave several candidates for the peak at {rt} min ({hits}); the standard file decides for "{target}".
footer.examples: Example data: compound sets and concentrations from Wang et al., Food Chem X 2025 (yogurt, CC BY-NC); Xu et al. (pasteurized milk, CC BY-NC); Duensing, Hinrichs & Schieberle (Gouda, CC BY). Everything else is simulated.

fl.title: Flavor interpretation
fl.intro: Only the targets found above are used. With quantified amounts (an amount column) the page computes OAV = amount / threshold; OAV >= 1 means the compound can be smelled in the sample. With only peak areas or relative contents it computes ROAV: the compound with the largest contribution is 100, the others are scaled by their content / threshold ratio to it. ROAV only shows relative contributions within the sample, not whether a compound can be smelled.
fl.note_oav: The peak table has an amount column, so OAV is computed; you can switch to ROAV.
fl.note_roav: The peak table has no amount column, so ROAV is computed from {basis}.
fl.basis_rel: the relative contents in the peak table
fl.unit_from_header: Unit taken from the column name "{col}"; please check.
fl.unit_default: The column name "{col}" has no unit; µg/kg is assumed, please check above.
thr.title: Odor thresholds
thr.intro: Odor thresholds of the {n} compounds found (converted to mg/kg); {miss} have none. Values from your standard file come first; where it has none, the built-in value is used (the 53 water thresholds already used by this site's Flavor Improver, cited in L.J. van Gemert (2011) Odour Thresholds, Part II). You can also change or add values here; your changes are kept in this browser only. Compounds without a threshold are not estimated and are left out.
thr.src_none: No built-in threshold, please enter one
rank.title: Key flavor compounds
rank.summary_oav: Of {n} compounds found, {key} have OAV >= 1 (can be smelled) and {mod} have OAV between 0.1 and 1; {miss} have no threshold or value and are listed at the end, not used.
rank.summary_roav: Of {n} compounds found, {key} have ROAV >= 1 (usually taken as key flavor compounds) and {mod} have ROAV between 0.1 and 1 (usually taken as modifying); {miss} have no threshold or value and are listed at the end, not used.
radar.title: Flavor profile
radar.note: Same rule as Flavor Improver: each compound's intensity I = log10({score}) (when {score} > 1, else 0) weights the GNN's odor label probabilities divided by each label's frequency in the training data (so common labels do not dominate); the {n} compounds are summed, the 12 dairy dimensions are taken and normalized, and the numbers are each dimension's share. Suited to dairy samples. The odor column above prefers knowledge-base data, but the profile needs one numeric scale, so it uses model predictions throughout.
radar.no_lift: These compounds are not in the flavor knowledge base, so they have no odor descriptors or model prediction and are not in the profile: {list}.
radar.none: No compound has an intensity above 0 and a model prediction, so there is no profile.
lim.title: Limitations
lim.1: This is a first screening based on identified compounds; it does not replace olfactometric checks such as GC-O or AEDA.
lim.2: Library search results can be misidentifications; the automatic rules (merging, closest peak) only assist, and your review decides.
lim.3: Thresholds vary greatly with the medium (water, oil, milk) and between studies, often by orders of magnitude for one compound, so the results depend on the thresholds in your standard file. The few built-in values are water thresholds; replace them with suitable values for other matrices.
lim.4: ROAV only shows relative contributions within the sample; OAV also ignores interactions such as synergy and masking.
lim.5: The odor labels in the profile come from this site's odor model (GNN); they are predictions, not measurements.
lim.6: Reference retention times depend on the column and method; the standard file must come from your own method.
footer.flavor: Thresholds and odors: your standard file's values first; built-in values are the 53 water thresholds already used by this site's Flavor Improver, cited in L.J. van Gemert (2011) Odour Thresholds, Part II, each with its original study; odor descriptors from Dunkel et al., Angew. Chem. 2014 and FlavorDB (Garg et al., NAR 2018, CC BY-NC-SA 3.0); model predictions from the GNN of this site's odor predictor, computed offline and loaded with the page.
radar.no_lift_link: You can enter their SMILES in this site's odor predictor to see the predicted odor.
rank.no_kb: Not in the knowledge base: enter the SMILES in the odor predictor
manual.intro: Peaks in the window that the library identified as something else and that no other target uses, closest to the reference RT first (library match in brackets). If you judge that one of them is actually this compound, click "Assign to this compound". Each peak can be assigned to one compound only.
log.manual: {target}: no peak with an agreeing identification in the window; you assigned the peak at {rt} min (library: {name}) to it.
std.required: The standard file needs three columns: (1) compound name or CAS number; (2) reference retention time; (3) odor threshold (give the unit in the column name, e.g. "Threshold (µg/kg)"). Thresholds are used for OAV/ROAV and the flavor profile; the site has only a few built-in values, so compounds with no threshold in the standard file and no built-in value are left out of the flavor calculation.
std.thr_unit_header: Unit taken from the column name "{col}"; please check.
std.thr_unit_default: The column name "{col}" has no unit; mg/kg is assumed, please choose the right unit on the left.
std.warn_no_thr: No odor threshold column: the flavor calculation can only use the few built-in thresholds, and most compounds will get no OAV/ROAV. Adding a threshold column to the standard file is recommended.
radar.note_all: Each compound's intensity I = log10({score}) (when {score} > 1, else 0) weights the GNN's probabilities for 138 odor labels (not divided by label frequency here: over 138 labels that would inflate rare labels such as cucumber a hundredfold); the {n} compounds are summed and normalized. The chart shows the 10 largest labels as percentages of the total. Suited to non-dairy samples. The profile uses model predictions throughout.
handoff.title: Compare with a target in Flavor Improver
handoff.intro: Saves this result in your browser (not uploaded) so you can compare it with a target in Flavor Improver.
handoff.failed: Could not save: local storage is unavailable in this browser, or there is nothing to send. Use "Export the ranking (CSV)" and upload the file in Flavor Improver instead.
hero.sub: Upload one sample's peak table and your target list; get the key flavor compounds, OAV/ROAV and a flavor profile.
std.short: Columns: name or CAS · reference RT (your own method) · odor threshold (unit in the header).
fl.intro_short: OAV when amounts are quantified; ROAV from peak areas (relative contribution within the sample only).
thr.intro_short: Thresholds of the {n} compounds found (mg/kg); {miss} have none. Your standard file first, then built-in water values (van Gemert 2011); edits stay in this browser.
radar.note_short: Profile from model-predicted odor labels of {n} compounds, weighted by log10({score}); 12 dairy dimensions.
radar.note_all_short: Profile from model-predicted odor labels of {n} compounds, weighted by log10({score}); 10 largest of 138 labels.
about.thr: Odor thresholds of the compounds found are converted to mg/kg. Values from your standard file come first; where it has none, the built-in value is used (the 53 water thresholds already used by this site's Flavor Improver, cited in L.J. van Gemert (2011) Odour Thresholds, Part II). You can also change or add values on the tool page; your changes are kept in your browser only. Compounds without a threshold are not estimated and are left out.
about.radar: 12 dairy dimensions (default), the same rule as Flavor Improver: each compound's intensity I = log10(OAV or ROAV) (when it is above 1, else 0) weights the GNN's odor label probabilities divided by each label's frequency in the training data (so common labels do not dominate); the compounds are summed, the 12 dairy dimensions are taken and normalized, and the numbers are each dimension's share. Suited to dairy samples. The odor column of the ranking prefers knowledge-base data, but the profile needs one numeric scale, so it uses model predictions throughout.
about.radar_all: All 138 odor labels: each compound's intensity I = log10(OAV or ROAV) (when it is above 1, else 0) weights the GNN's probabilities for 138 odor labels (not divided by label frequency here: over 138 labels that would inflate rare labels such as cucumber a hundredfold); the compounds are summed and normalized. The chart shows the 10 largest labels as percentages of the total. Suited to non-dairy samples. The profile uses model predictions throughout.
footer.short: Everything runs in your browser. Odor labels come from this site's odor model (CC BY-NC, non-commercial academic demo only). See method & sources.
about.basis_area: ROAV from peak areas is equivalent to using area-normalized relative contents, without rounding.
